Rashi on Arakhin 34a:1:1.english: They and their open lots - when they are surrounded by a wall:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:1:2.hebrew: והא למיסתרינהו קיימי - כדאמר (לעיל ערכין דף לג:): אין עושין אותן טירין וכרכים:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:1:2.english: But they stand to be dismantled - as it is stated (above, Arakhin 33b): one may not make them [into] fortresses or walled cities:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:1:3.hebrew: סד"א אדמסתתרי - כל זמן שלא נסתרו, אם מכרום קודם סתירתן, ליחלטו; קמ"ל:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:1:3.english: It might enter your mind to say: While they are [yet to be] dismantled - as long as they have not been dismantled, if they sold [the houses] prior to their dismantling, let them be [the buyer's] in perpetuity; [therefore, the baraita] teaches us [that this is not the case]:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:2:1.hebrew: מה ת"ל - "כשדה החרם", מה בא "שדה החרם" ללמד על שדה היוצאת לכהנים ביובל:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:2:1.english: What does the verse teach - [Meaning,] "as a field dedicated": what does "a field dedicated" come to teach regarding a field that goes out to the priests in the Jubilee:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:2:2.english: His dedicated field - A field that an Israelite dedicated and [which] came to his portion:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:2:3.hebrew: הואיל ויוצאה לכהנים - אם לא יגאלנה, שהרי היא שלו כשדה אחוזה, ועכשיו הרי היא תחת ידי כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:2:3.english: Since it goes out to the priests - [i.e.,] if he does not redeem it, for it is his like an ancestral field, and now behold it is in my possession, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:3:1.hebrew: בשל אחרים אני זוכה - אם היה שדה אחוזת ישראל יוצאה לכהנים ביובל, היה לי חלק בה:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:3:1.english: I acquire [the fields] of others - If an ancestral field of an Israelite were to go out to the priests in the Jubilee [year], I would have a share in it:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:4:1.hebrew: מה שדה אחוזה של ישראל - אם גאלה כהן מיד הקדש, יוצאה מידו ביובל ומתחלקת לכל אחיו הכהנים, כדאמר באידך פירקא בפרק אין מקדישין (לעיל ערכין דף כה:), אף זו כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:4:1.english: Just as the ancestral field of an Israelite - If a priest redeemed it from the Temple treasury, it leaves his possession at the Jubilee and is divided among all his brothers, the priests, as was stated in the other chapter, in the chapter [entitled] Ein Makdishin (above, Arakhin 25b), so too this [dedicated field], etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:6:1.hebrew: ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו - ודרשינן ליה בהגוזל בב"ק (דף קט:): מנין לכהן שבא ומקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה — אם יש עליו להביא חטאת, או התנדב עולה או שלמים, אין צריך לתתם לאנשי משמר, אלא הוא עצמו מקריב ויטול העור ואוכל הבשר? ת"ל: "ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו":
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:6:1.english: And every man's hallowed things shall be his - And we expound it in [the chapter] HaGozel in Bava Kamma (109b): From where [do we derive] regarding a priest who comes and offers his sacrifices at any time and at any hour that he wishes — [such as] if he is obligated to bring a sin-offering, or he volunteered a burnt-offering or a peace-offering, he does not need to give them to the members of the [priestly] watch, rather he himself offers [them], and takes the hide, and eats the meat? The verse states: "And every man's hallowed things shall be his":

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:7:1.hebrew: קדשיו לאו ברשותו - ולאו מכח דידיה קא שקיל להו, אלא מקריב אימוריהם:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:7:1.english: His hallowed things are not in his possession - And he does not take them by his own right, rather he [merely] offers their sacrificial parts:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:7:2.hebrew: הכא ברשותו - כלומר, מכח דידיה קא שקיל להו, ולא משלחן גבוה בשכר עבודה:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:7:2.english: Here, [it is in] his possession - That is to say, he takes them by virtue of his own [right], and not from the table of the Most High as payment for [Temple] service:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:8:1.hebrew: אלא אמר ר"נ - להכי איצטריך למכתב "החרם", דסד"א כו', והאי נמי אחוזתו היא, ואם הקדישה ולא גאלה, לא תצא לכהנים ביובל, אלא יהא לו רשות לגאלה לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:8:1.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said - For this [reason] it was necessary to write "the dedicated [field]," for it might have entered your mind [to say], etc., that this too is his ancestral [field], and if he consecrated it and did not redeem it, it would not go out to the priests in the Jubilee, rather he would have the right to redeem it forever:

Rashi on Arakhin 34a:8:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - היקש דאיתקש שדה החרם לשדה אחוזתו של ישראל, דתצא מתחת ידו ותתחלק לכהנים; דאחוזתו היא דיש לה גאולת עולם, אבל חרמו לא הויא כאחוזה ליגאל לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 34a:8:2.english: It teaches us - [the] juxtaposition whereby the dedicated field is compared to the ancestral field of an Israelite [teaches] that it leaves his possession and is divided among the priests; for [it is] his ancestral field that has perpetual redemption, whereas his dedicated field is not like an ancestral field to be redeemed forever:

Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:1:1.hebrew: הן ומגרשיהן למיסתרינהו קיימי - וא"ת: מאי נפקא מינה אם נסתרו, כיון שהיו מוקפות חומה מעיקרא? דהא תניא לעיל: "אשר לו חומה" — ואע"פ שאין לו עכשיו, והיה לו קודם לכן! ושמא י"ל דאתיא כרבי אלעזר בר' יוסי, ושאני הכא: כיון שהם ראויות שלא יהא להם חומה, לא תועיל להם קדושת חומה שהיה קודם לכן, כאילו לא היתה מעולם:
Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:1:1.english: They and their open spaces stand to be dismantled - And if you ask: What difference does it make if they were dismantled, since they were surrounded by a wall originally? For it was taught above: "[A house in a city] that has a wall" — even though it does not have [one] now, [as long as] it had [one] previously! Perhaps one can say that [this] follows Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Yose, and here it is different: since they are fit not to have a wall, the sanctity of a wall that existed previously does not avail them, [and it is] as if it had never existed at all:

Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:5:1.hebrew: מי דמי התם זוכה - והכא נמי הוי מצי למיפרך: כשהוא זוכה בשל אחרים, והוי במשמר שלו, אבל הכא רצה לזכות משמר אחר, והיא אינה מתחלקת לכהנים של משמר אחר, כדפי' לעיל (ערכין דף כה.); אלא דעדיפא מינה פריך, שאפילו באה משמרתו כשיוצאה לכהנים, אין לזכות מהאי קל וחומר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:5:1.english: Are [they] comparable? There he acquires - Here too, [the Gemara] could have objected: when he acquires [a field] of others, it is in his own watch, whereas here he wants to acquire [it even during] another watch, and it is not divided among the priests of another watch, as we explained above (Arakhin 25a); rather, [the Gemara] raises a stronger [objection] than that: that even when his watch arrives when [the field] goes out to the priests, he cannot acquire [it] from this a fortiori inference:

Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רמי בר חמא איצטריך כו' [אלא] אמר רב נחמן [איצטריך] ס"ד כו' - ואם תאמר: מאי היא דנאמר "ודין הוא"? והלא אין לנו לומר שזוכה בו מטעם קל וחומר, אלא מטעם דכתיבי קראי — ד"איש כי יקדיש" לרמי בר חמא, ו"לאחוזת עולם" לרב נחמן! וי"ל דמכל מקום ניחא ליה לאיתויי קל וחומר כך מסברא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:6:1.english: Rami bar Ḥama said: It was necessary, etc.; [rather,] Rav Naḥman said: [It was necessary,] it might enter your mind [to say], etc. - And if you ask: What is [the meaning of] that which [the baraita] says, "And this is [based on] logical inference"? After all, we do not say that he acquires it by reason of an a fortiori argument, but rather by reason of the verses that are written — "If a man consecrates" according to Rami bar Ḥama, and "for a perpetual possession" according to Rav Naḥman! One can answer that nevertheless, it was pleasing to [the Tanna] to adduce an a fortiori argument like this from logical reasoning:

Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:8:1.hebrew: הא קא משמע לן אחוזתו אחוזתו אין חרמו לא - ואם תאמר: הא לעיל ילפינן מהקישא דמקיש שדה חרמו לשדה אחוזה לישראל, ואמאי דריש ליה הכא מאחוזתו? ויש לומר דהכי פירושו: קא משמע לן מאחוזתו של כהן, דאחוזתו דוקא יש לה גאולת עולם ואינה מתחלקת לכהנים ביובל, אבל שדה חרמו מתחלק לכהנים ביובל מהיקשא דמקשינן ליה לשדה אחוזה של ישראל, ולא הויא כשדה אחוזתו ליגאל לעולם. וכן פרש"י:
Tosafot on Arakhin 34a:8:1.english: This teaches us: his ancestral [field] — his ancestral [field], yes; his dedicated [field], no - And if you will say: Behold, above we derived from the hekkesh [scriptural juxtaposition] that [the verse] juxtaposes his dedicated field to an ancestral field of an Israelite, so why does [the Gemara] derive it here from "his ancestral [field]"? And one can say that this is its explanation: [The Gemara] teaches us from "his ancestral [field]" of a priest, that specifically his ancestral [field] has perpetual redemption and is not divided among the priests in the Jubilee, whereas his dedicated field is divided among the priests in the Jubilee [as derived] from the hekkesh wherein we juxtapose it to an ancestral field of an Israelite, and it is not like his ancestral field to be redeemed perpetually. And so Rashi explained:
